correctness.rationale: For the exact 15-vertex Kneser graph KG(6,2), the closed radius-one nerve has 15 seven-vertex facets and 1535 nonempty faces. A deterministic staged face-toggle matching pairs 735 disjoint codimension-one incidences, with one critical vertex and 64 critical 2-faces; a topological sort verifies all 5985 oriented Hasse incidences form a directed acyclic graph. Forman discrete Morse gives a CW complex with one point and 64 two-cells, necessarily a wedge of 64 two-spheres. Independent F2 boundary ranks agree, but the integral conclusion uses the Morse proof. The S6 character follows by signed Lefschetz fixed-face enumeration across all 11 conjugacy classes and exact Murnaghan–Nakayama inner products, with seven distinct Specht types of total dimension 64. The self-contained code verify.py was executed successfully and printed VERIFY_OK. No claim extends to other Kneser graphs or an integral equivariant decomposition.

value.rationale: KG(6,2) is the smallest triangle-bearing Kneser graph KG(n,2) after the Petersen case and is a natural first threshold example at scale two outside the girth-controlled graph recovery regime. The exact integral homotopy type and complete rational symmetry character provide a motivated structural classification; the seven distinct Specht summands are stronger than Betti numbers and help distinguish open versus closed neighborhood topology. No arbitrary parameter tuning or downstream application is required for this precise invariant to be mathematically meaningful.
